⚡ **Protocol Call Resources:**

🔗 **Zoom**: Custom meeting link (see issue description)
✅ **Calendar**: [View](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=c_upaofong8mgrmrkegn7ic7hk5s%40group.calendar.google.com&ctz=UTC&mode=AGENDA&dates=20260603%2F20260604&showTitle=1&showCalendars=0&showTabs=0&showPrint=0&showNav=0) | [Add to Calendar](https://www.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE&text=EIPIP+Meeting+%23127%2C+June+03%2C+2026&dates=20260603T160000Z%2F20260603T170000Z&details=Issue%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fethereum%2Fpm%2Fissues%2F2086)
✅ **Discourse**: [Discussion Topic](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/28644)

I want to put https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11744/changes on agenda, not the contents, but the general policy regarding authorship changes. The EIP changes:

```diff
-author: Greg Colvin <greg@colvin.org>, Martin Holst Swende (@holiman), Brooklyn Zelenka (@expede), John Max Skaller <skaller@internode.on.net>
+author: Greg Colvin <greg@colvin.org>, Greg Colvin (@gcolvin), Martin Holst Swende, Brooklyn Zelenka, John Max Skaller
```

I want to discuss our current "rules" and what applies here. If Greg Colvin can sign this (as original author) via the original email (how?) then merging the changes to the EIP should not be a problem (the removal of the emails/usernames likely is though?)

Another item: when doing editorial reviews of EIPs/ERCs, it is clear (to me) we should do be oldest-first (longest waiting first). 

However, this raises the question if we could prioritize some PRs earlier. For instance, above PR  https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11744/changes is intended to be discussed tomorrow. For clarity in the ACD process it is therefore (my opinion) a logical choice to handle these PRs over other pending PRs first. This ensures that the ACD governance process does not point to a PR, but rather to the current state of the EIP on https://eips.ethereum.org.

However, this has some problems: it needs a communication channel from the EIP author to EIP editors, which is easier if authors "know" these people (e.g. via discord or personally). The second problem (which might be artificial) is that this would open a route to prioritize EIP editor reviews by just adding them to an ACD agenda, which is not what we want (could be seen as somewhat "spammy").

Would like to discuss the current thought model of this and how we can integrate these prioritizations in the process, and if we want this, and this especially in the perspective of EIPs for the "current next" fork (Glamsterdam) and the "fork after" (Hegota). (Note that these are both agenda items on ACD, which could be a guideline to do prio-reviews?)

EIPs WG: https://github.com/eips-wg/

The preprocessor repo is the centerpiece powering the system: https://github.com/eips-wg/preprocessor/
Current system in the review pipeline spanning 5 repos: https://github.com/eips-wg/preprocessor/issues/15

Latest version of my fork that includes many non-merged PRs / features still in the review pipeline: https://wg-eips.ritovision.com/
This meeting occurred more than 24 hours ago. Closing automatically.
